text: dsh-novel-solo 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的小说写作插件，提供子 agent 数量设置卡片和「单核写作主理」预设。用户可将并发上限设为 1 到 12；设置会保存在宿主配置并镜像到本机文件，预设加载时据此调整写作规则。预设按叙事方法、世界观、名词索引、大纲、章节目录、人物档案到逐章写作与审核的流程组织任务，并提供章节审查和全书终审要求。插件兼容不同宿主设置接口，旧版宿主会部署随包预设；预设还收紧模型工具组合并为 llama 固定 toolChoice。安装后从插件页调整数量，改动需要重启宿主才会进入写作提示。

dsh-novel-solo adds a novel-writing preset and a DSH web settings card for a subagent cap of 1–12. The preset guides planning, drafting, chapter reviews and final review. The setting is mirrored for use at preset load, so restart the host after changing it.
我想在 DSH 里按步骤规划和写一部长篇小说。
能不能给小说章节安排独立审核，再做全书终审？
想控制写作流程里同时派出的子 agent 数量。
让 DSH 帮我维护大纲、章节目录和人物档案。
小模型写小说时，我想减少可用工具并限制输出格式。
我调了代理并发设置，怎样让写作提示按新值更新？
I need a DSH workflow for planning, drafting, and reviewing a novel chapter by chapter.
How can I set a parallel subagent limit for a writing preset?
dsh-novel-solo 的功能「子 agent 并发设置」：在插件页用数字输入框设定 1–12 的并发上限，保存到宿主设置。插件将其镜像到本地文件，预设加载时据此更新写作提示。
dsh-novel-solo 的功能「小说创作流程」：挂载预设后按叙事方法、世界观、名词索引、大纲、章节目录、人物档案和逐章正文组织创作，并要求章节审核与全书终审。
dsh-novel-solo 的功能「宿主兼容配置」：节点端根据宿主版本选择旧版预设部署或新版设置表单路径；浏览器端分别注册旧设置页和新版 Plugins 页卡片。
dsh-novel-solo 的功能「小说预设工具组合」：预设加载写作 persona，保留文件编辑、搜索与子 agent 等工具，并关闭 bash、web 等指定工具；内置插件会为 llama 请求设置 toolChoice。
dsh-novel-solo 使用前须知：更改并发数量后需重启宿主，设置镜像和 persona 都在加载时读取，界面改值不会即时更新写作提示。（见 lib/index.js:129-131）
dsh-novel-solo 使用前须知：并发数写入 DSH_HOME 下的 .dsh-novel-solo-data/agent-count.json；未设置时用 ~/.dsh。（见 lib/index.js:37-39、95-103）

dsh-novel-solo README · dsh-novel-solo：A **single-author novel-writing plugin** for DeepSeek Harness: a **subagent concurrency setting** plus a **complete novel-creation preset** (persona). It is tuned for quantized small models — the tool catalog is slimmed and output behavior hardened — so you can run a full-length novel pipeline locally.

dsh-novel-solo README · Features：- **GUI setting**: a "Subagent count (1-12)" card on the plugin page (0.1.7: left rail → Plugins; 0.1.6: Settings → Plugins), with built-in zh/en i18n.
- **Full creation preset**: ships the `novel-solo` preset with a self-driven persona that follows a fixed pipeline — 叙事方法 (narrative method) → 核心世界观 (core worldview) → 名词索引 (noun index) → 大纲 (outline) → 章节目录 (chapter list) → 人物档案 (character files) → chapter-by-chapter writing → per-chapter review → final whole-book review & assembly.
- **Quantized-safe protocol**: plain CJK + common punctuation only, no JSON, no escapes, avoids fragile tokens; minimal tool calls, one at a time.
- **Review loop**: every chapter is reviewed (green/yellow/red) across 7 dimensions (setting / character / catalog / narrative / text rules / AI-cliché / plot logic); each report is written to a markdown file; when all chapters pass, a whole-book review runs and the book is assembled.
- **No AI clichés**: judges AI-flavor across six dimensions (sentence templates / stock vocabulary / emotion telling / structural sameness / diluted information / character distortion), distinguishing narrator-level repetition from character-leve

dsh-novel-solo README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add "dsh-novel-solo"
dsh web
```

Then open the plugin page — **Plugins** in the left rail on 0.1.7, **Settings → Plugins** on 0.1.6 — and the dsh-novel-solo "Subagent count" card appears.

dsh-novel-solo README · Install：On hosts older than 0.1.7 the plugin additionally **deploys the preset idempotently** from `template/` to `<dshHome>/.agent-presets/novel-solo/`, because that was the only preset contract there (an existing target is skipped — your edited preset is never overwritten). On 0.1.7 nothing is deployed: the preset arrives as a declarative row in the profile patch.

dsh-novel-solo README · Host compatibility：The plugin supports **DSH `0.1.6-alpha.1` / `0.1.6-alpha.2` and, from `0.1.7-alpha.1` on, every later host release** and picks its route per host. Both halves probe the host's own version through `ctx.profileContext.installAnchor` — the YAML `disabled:` gate in `cordis.patch.yml` and the same check in `lib/index.js` — and fall back to the 0.1.6 route whenever the version cannot be read. Everything from 0.1.7 on takes the same route, 0.2.0 included.

dsh-novel-solo README · Host compatibility：| | 0.1.6 | 0.1.7 and later |
|---|---|---|
| Preset delivery | deploy `template/` into `<dshHome>/.agent-presets/novel-solo/` | declarative `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row in the patch |
| Where `N` is saved | `dsh-novel-solo` settings namespace the plugin registers | the plugin's own `Config` (`count` is `volatile`), projected into the profile patch |
| Card slot | `settings.plugin.item` via `settingsScope` | `plugins.item` via `configForms` |

dsh-novel-solo README · Host compatibility：Both routes are exercised against a real host; the 0.1.7 one on `0.1.7-rc.1` (card renders on the Plugins page, saves land in `cordis.patch.yml`, preset shows up in the picker). The 0.1.6 route is covered by the same version gate offline, since no 0.1.6 host binary is installed next to the 0.1.7 one. The hosts actually installed here now are `0.2.0-rc.1`, `0.2.1-alpha.3` and `0.2.1-rc.2`, and both plugins were installed and booted side by side on each: the node half runs (the `.dsh-novel-solo-data` mirror is still written), `--dump-config` shows both declaration rows and the `novel-solo` roster id, and nothing gets force-disabled. The card itself was not re-clicked in a 0.2.1 browser, but every seam it rides on was checked against the host source at `0.2.1-rc.2` — the `plugins.item` slot, `configForms.get` / `whileServed`, `settings.configure` / `update`, the client manifest's `id`/`url`/`rev`, and `bind` / `register` on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-locale` — all identical to `0.1.7-rc.1`; the same seam list was re-read at `0.2.1-rc.3` and none of it moved (the plugin-manager page only gained an additive `openList()` reflection method for the

dsh-novel-solo README · Host compatibility：Four 0.2.x changes this package has caught up with: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-worker-thread` was folded into the PTC engine, so that row is now `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workflow-ptc` (still `disabled: true`); `tool-subagent` dropped `backgroundMode` and `enableRunInBackground` (they no longer error, they simply do nothing, so they were removed); and since 0.2.x a browser only loads a client graph whose release matches the host's, so after a host upgrade the page must be reloaded before the card re-mounts. The fourth is how the persona is interpolated: since 0.2.1 the host resolves `{{…}}` **strictly**, and an unregistered name throws `unknown prompt variable ... in section "deployment:persona-prefix"`. The persona's `{{cwd}}` was never a host variable — the whole host registers only `provider` and `model` — so the preset row failed to load and no message could be sent at all (issue #2). It no longer depends on template variables: the working directory comes from the required `Current working directory` entry in the runtime context (neither `complete` nor `includeRuntimeContext` suppresses a required contribution), and an absolute path is one `wo

dsh-novel-solo README · Host compatibility：On `0.2.2-alpha.2` one thing moved that this preset does touch: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent-control/list-agents` **no longer exists as a subpath export** — the `list_agents` tool was folded into that package's main entry, and factory `standard` deleted its own `tool-subagent-list-agents` row in the same release. The row is therefore probed rather than declared: `disabled` resolves the subpath and switches the row off when it cannot be found, which keeps the tool on 0.2.1 and avoids a duplicate registration on 0.2.2. A `disabled` row is filtered before the Loader resolves any package name, so a host without the subpath loses nothing else. Two 0.2.2 facts that do **not** reach this package: `tool-subagent` renamed `modelSelectionSettings` to `modelSelection` (this preset never set that key), and `{{…}}` interpolation itself is unchanged — the persona no longer references any template variable, so the registered-variable set is not something this preset depends on. `template/agent.cordis.yml` is the single source for the whole row list: `cordis.patch.yml`'s generated region is produced from it by `node scripts/sync-preset-patch.mjs`, so t

dsh-novel-solo README · Host compatibility：Whether the plugin loads at all is decided before its code runs: since `0.1.7-rc.1` the host evaluates every `@deepseek-ai/dsh*` range in `peerDependencies` against the running release and disables the row if one of them doesn't match, and since `0.2.1-alpha.4` it consults `engines.dsh` first — once that field exists it decides the verdict alone and `peerDependencies` no longer participates (each rule was tested against the host code of `0.2.1-alpha.3` and `0.2.1-rc.2` respectively). So both lists are kept: they name `0.1.6-alpha.1` through `0.2.2-alpha.2`, then end in an open arm — `>=0.1.7-alpha.1`, with no upper bound — because nothing in this plugin is bound to a particular host build: its route is chosen by its own version gate at load time, so an unchecked release should still get a working plugin rather than lose one to a check that fails closed. The versions named before the open arm are the ones that were actually compared. The umbrella does not promise behavior across a contract change: the declarative preset row is the part a future host would break first, and the fix for that belongs in the patch file, not in the range — and li

dsh-novel-solo README · Host compatibility：Since `0.1.5`, the persona uses the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona` config key `prefix` (the `text` key of 0.1.2-rc.1 was removed), so hosts older than that need the persona row renamed by hand. Each home keeps its own deployed copy; homes provisioned by older hosts keep their `text:` copy and still work when you switch back.

dsh-novel-solo README · How the subagent count takes effect：DSH's `agent/request` waterfall only lets a plugin rewrite LLM routing/config — it cannot inject or rewrite `system`/`messages` — so "GUI → model prompt" dynamic injection cannot go through the request waterfall. This plugin wires the value through files instead:
section: How the subagent count takes effect

text:
dsh-novel-solo README · How the subagent count takes effect：1. The card saves `N` into the host's settings store (see the table above). That is the source of truth.
2. On load, the node half mirrors it to `<dshHome>/.dsh-novel-solo-data/agent-count.json`.
3. The persona row resolves `!!js` while the preset loads: it reads `template/persona.md` and replaces that file's `并发上限 N=<number>` anchor with the mirrored number. The persona then decides: `N=1` the main agent does everything itself; `N>1` writing/review tasks are delegated to subagents while the main agent only dispatches and silently waits.
section: How the subagent count takes effect

text: dsh-novel-solo README · How the subagent count takes effect：> Note: the mirror and the persona are both resolved while the host loads its plugins, so **a GUI change reaches the prompt only after a host restart**. Volatile settings give the node side no change callback, so there is nothing to push the new value out live.

text: dsh-novel-solo README · Preset at a glance：The persona body lives in `template/persona.md`; `template/agent.cordis.yml` (mirrored into `cordis.patch.yml`) carries the tool rows around it. Content:

dsh-novel-solo README · Preset at a glance：| Section | Content |
|---|---|
| Division of labor | concurrency anchor `N=1` (default), with N=1 / N>1 execution paths |
| Quantized-safe rules | top-priority constraints on output and tool calls |
| Six-doc standard structures | per-field templates for 叙事方法 / 核心世界观 / 名词索引 / 大纲 / 章节目录 / 人物档案 |
| Writing & review rules | chapter rules, AI-cliché lists, A–G review dimensions + green/yellow/red, md review reports, whole-book review & assembly |
| Tool usage standards | per-tool rules for read/write/edit/glob/grep/subagent, etc. |
| Project & discipline | the project dir is the `项目名` folder under the working directory; paths come from the runtime context's Current working directory or the `working_directory` tool — never from a template variable — one thing at a time |

dsh-novel-solo README · Tool slimming：The preset hard-disables these rows via `disabled: true`: `tool-bash`, `tool-jobs`, `skill-filesystem`, `tool-skill`, `tool-goal`, `plan-mode`, `subagent_codex`, `subagent_claude_code`, `workflow-ptc`, `tool-workflow`, `tool-ralph`, `tool-todo`, `tool-web`. It keeps `tool-fs` (read/write/edit, with `read_image` switched off), `tool-fs-search` (glob/grep), `str-replace-editor` (view/create/str_replace/insert), `tool-pwsh` (filesystem management only: rename/delete files & folders), `subagent`/`subagent_fork`, `list_agents`, etc.

dsh-novel-solo README · Tool slimming：0.2.1's `standard` preset grew four more model-facing toolchains, and this preset screens every one of them out: `tool-schedule` (cron tasks), `command-goal` (the `/goal` command), `tool-present` (deliverable presentation), and the `tools` entry of `plugin-manager` / `plugin-market`. They are spelled out as `disabled: true` rows — a preset's `plugins` is a complete composition, so an unlisted row is already absent, but the host itself disables rather than deletes on the web layer because an omitted row quietly reappears the day someone reorders the composition; and `disabled` rows are filtered before name resolution, so an older host without those packages is never killed by them. Two prompt-only rows are simply left out: `agent-instructions` (AGENTS.md injection) and `time-context` (clock context) would be dead weight under `complete: true`.

dsh-novel-solo README · Tool slimming：One thing the preset cannot govern: the `working_directory` tool is a host-plane row every session receives, so the persona treats it as the source of truth for paths instead of fighting it.

It also ships a **preset-scoped** vendored plugin (active only for sessions mounting the `novel-solo` preset):

dsh-novel-solo README · Tool slimming：- `template/plugins/llm-tool-choice-pin/index.mjs`, exported as `dsh-novel-solo/plugins` — pins `toolChoice` to `auto` for the `llama` provider so retained tools like `edit` stay callable (avoids per-request tool decisions under small models).

dsh-novel-solo README · File structure：```
lib/index.js        node half: host version gate, count mirror, settings seam (0.1.7 volatile `Config` form / 0.1.6 namespace), preset deploy on legacy hosts
lib/client.js       browser half: the "Subagent count" card, mounted on `plugins.item` (0.1.7) and `settings.plugin.item` (0.1.6)
cordis.patch.yml    installed into the web profile: the plugin row plus the declarative novel-solo preset row (disabled below 0.1.7)
cordis.yml          development overlay: card only, no preset rows

dsh-novel-solo README · File structure：`npm run check` syntax-checks both halves, re-runs the patch/template consistency check, and rejects any `{{variable}}` in `template/persona.md` that the host does not register (only `provider` / `model` exist; one wrong name is a load-time failure, not a cosmetic gap in the UI).

dsh-novel-solo README · Environment variables：| Variable | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `DSH_HOME` | dsh home directory | `~/.dsh` |
| `DSH_NOVEL_SKIP_DEPLOY` | `1` skips preset deployment (legacy hosts only) | none |
| `DSH_NOVEL_REDEPLOY` | `1` forcibly overwrites an existing preset (use with care) | none |

dsh-novel-solo README · Test environment：This plugin was tested end-to-end with a local model:

- **Runtime**: llama.cpp (`llama-b10615-bin-win-cuda-13.3-x64`)
- **Model**: `Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-Uncensored-HauhauCS-Aggressive-IQ4_XS.gguf`
- **Context**: `ctx=65536`, `reasoning on`
- **Hardware**: laptop RTX 4060 8GB + 32GB RAM + AMD 7840H CPU
- **Measured on a ~10k-char novel**: 22 token/s, 98% cache hit; 78.8k input / 36.9k output / 2.3M cache; 22 turns / 63 steps, 1h03m42s total

**Key server flags (llama-server)**:

dsh-novel-solo README · Test environment：```sh
llama-server.exe -m <model.gguf> --no-mmproj --load-mode none --n-cpu-moe 30 -c 65536 -ngl 999 -t 12 -b 1024 -ub 512 -ctk q8_0 -ctv q8_0 -fa on --fit off --no-warmup --poll 0 --temp 0.85 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 --min-p 0.05 --repeat-penalty 1.35 --presence-penalty 0.2 --frequency-penalty 0.2 --dry-multiplier 0.8 --dry-base 1.75 --jinja --reasoning on --reasoning-effort medium --reasoning-budget 2048 --reasoning-format deepseek --reasoning-preserve --cont-batching -np 1 --alias "qwen3.6-novel-nsfw-reason" --port 8090 --host 127.0.0.1 --ui --keep -1 --cache-ram 4096 --ctx-checkpoints 64
```
